author: high
claim: Let (G) be a finite connected undirected graph with at least one edge. Suppose every vertex of (G) has even degree. Prove that (G) has a closed trail that traverses every edge exactly once.

verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and self-contained. It constructs a nonempty closed trail by a finite greedy process and an endpoint-incidence parity argument, chooses a maximal closed trail, proves the residual graph has even degrees, finds a residual closed trail meeting the maximal trail, and splices the two edge-disjoint trails to contradict maximality unless every edge is used. The reasoning also correctly accommodates loops through incidence counting. No external references or prohibited justification patterns occur.
